answer: A registry can forge each agent identity only after the agent locks a refundable stake that peers can slash on proof of duplicate accounts. Newcomers enter through a bridge: an established agent vouches for them and shares liability for the stake, so spawning many fake identities costs real capital per identity. The stake is tagged saffron while probationary, earning no reputation until the agent completes a season of verified work, which makes bulk fake accounts expensive and slow to weaponize.
